design_rationale: The study is a randomized controlled trial where participants were assigned randomly (1:1:1) to RT, ET, or SC using a computer-generated program with allocation concealment executed by a clinical research unit.

domain_judgments.rationale: Randomization sequence was generated by a computer program, allocation was concealed by the clinical research unit, and baseline characteristics were comparable across groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: After baseline assessments, the patients were assigned randomly (1:1:1) to RT, ET or SC using a computer-generated program. The allocation sequence was executed by the clinical research unit and concealed from the project team.

domain_judgments.rationale: A per-protocol approach was used excluding participants who attended <70% of sessions or dropped out (14/81 excluded, differentially between ET [9] and SC [2]), rather than an intention-to-treat analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The analyses included data of patients who attended a minimum of 70% of the training sessions according to protocol... Due to chemotherapy-related side-effects or withdrawal of consent, 14 out of 81 patients dropped out: three withdrew from the RT, nine from the ET and two from the SC groups. The data of 67 patients were fully evaluable

domain_judgments.rationale: Substantial (17.3%) missing outcome data occurred with marked imbalance across arms (ET: 31% dropout vs SC: 7% dropout), primarily related to health and side-effects, introducing high risk of attrition bias.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Due to chemotherapy-related side-effects or withdrawal of consent, 14 out of 81 patients dropped out: three withdrew from the RT, nine from the ET and two from the SC groups. The data of 67 patients were fully evaluable (21 patients in the RT, 20 in the ET and 26 in the SC groups).

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes included subjective, self-reported measures (quality of life, perceived exertion, fatigue) in an unblinded trial where participants were aware of their exercise assignment, with no mention of outcome assessor blinding for physical tests.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Primary end-points of this trial were muscular strength in newton meters at latissimus pull down, bench press and leg press, endurance, and subjective perceived exertion during endurance stress test (Borg scale) and QoL assessed using measured by standardized report form of the European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer (EORTC QLQ) C30+BR23 at T1 and T2.

domain_judgments.rationale: No prospective trial registry or pre-published statistical analysis plan was provided, and numerous scales, subscales, and physiological endpoints were evaluated across multiple analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study was approved by the Local Review Board (registration number: AZ A 157/11). All participants gave their written informed consent prior to enrollment in the study.

overall_summary: The study has a high overall risk of bias primarily due to exclusions from analysis violating intention-to-treat principles (per-protocol analysis requiring 70% attendance) and substantial, differential attrition across intervention groups (Domain 2 and Domain 3).

design_rationale: Participants were randomly allocated 1:1 to the exercise group or relaxation control group using predetermined lists with random block sizes generated by an independent biometrician.

domain_judgments.rationale: The random sequence generation was computer-generated with random block sizes, allocation was concealed via an independent biometrician, and baseline characteristics were balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Allocation was done by a biometrician who was not involved in the recruitment procedure, based on predetermined lists with a random block size, stratified by age and baseline physical fatigue level. Study personnel did not have access to the randomization lists.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although blinding of participants to behavioral exercise vs relaxation was not feasible, an active control was used, adherence was balanced, no major protocol deviations were reported, and analysis was conducted on an intention-to-treat basis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Data were analyzed on the intent-to-treat (ITT) basis. Analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) was used with pre- to postintervention change as dependent variable, the intervention group as independent variable, and the baseline measure as covariate.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data for the primary endpoint were available for 97% of participants (155 of 160 randomized), with very low and balanced missingness (3 in EX, 2 in RC).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Pre- and postintervention assessment of the primary end point was available in a total of 155 (97%) participants, 77 in EX and 78 in RC.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome is self-reported fatigue assessed by participants who were aware of their intervention group assignment in an unblinded trial, introducing some potential for subjective reporting bias.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary end point was change of cancer-related fatigue from baseline to week 13. Fatigue was assessed with the Fatigue Assessment Questionnaire (FAQ), a 20-item, self-assessment questionnaire validated for a German-speaking population [13].

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered (NCT01468766) and the published protocol predefined the primary outcome of fatigue, with analysis and reporting fully conforming to the prespecified plan.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary end point was change of cancer-related fatigue from baseline to week 13... The study was approved by the ethics committee of the University of Heidelberg and registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT01468766). Details of the study design are described elsewhere [12].

overall_summary: The overall judgment is some concerns, driven solely by the subjective, patient-reported nature of the primary fatigue outcome in an open-label behavioral trial where participants could not be blinded to their assigned intervention. All other domains demonstrated rigorous methodology and low risk of bias.

design_rationale: Participants were allocated to intervention or control groups via computer randomization stratified by study site and BMI.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation sequence was generated by computer randomization with stratification and block sizes of 6, baseline characteristics were well-balanced across groups, and test assessors/statisticians were blinded.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Results were entered into an online, secured database, and computer randomization allocated participants to either the intervention or the control, stratified by study site and a BMI > 30 kg/m2, in block sizes of 6.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although blinding of participants is not feasible in an exercise trial, analysis was conducted according to intention-to-treat principles, and contamination or deviations reflected pragmatic usual care without indication of biased non-adherence.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The usual-care group received no intervention but was allowed to exercise and to participate in municipality-led rehabilitation programs without restrictions... Analyses of effects included t tests and regression models; missing data were addressed by multiple imputation.

domain_judgments.rationale: Follow-up rates were high with minimal balanced dropout between groups, multiple imputation was used, and sensitivity analyses (best/worst case scenarios) showed consistent results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Missing data were addressed with multiple imputation, with age and education as auxiliary variables. In sensitivity analyses, we assessed the effect in complete cases, the possible effect of dropouts with worst and best case scenarios... Figure 2 shows 76 control and 82 intervention, with small and balanced loss to follow-up.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome of arm volume was measured using water displacement by physiotherapists who were explicitly blinded to group allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Measurements were made at the baseline and at a 12-month follow-up by physiotherapists blinded to group allocation... The testers, the dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) data collector (B.Z.), and the statistician (E.W.A.) were blinded to the group status.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered at ClinicalTrials.gov, and outcomes and predefined statistical models were reported consistently with the trial protocol.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: LYCA was approved by the ethics committee of the Capital Region of Denmark (H-15002714) and was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT02518477) before recruitment.

overall_summary: The study is a well-designed, pre-registered randomized trial with centralized computer randomization, blinded outcome assessors and statisticians, low loss to follow-up addressed with multiple imputation, and appropriate intention-to-treat analyses, resulting in an overall low risk of bias.

design_rationale: The study is described as a randomized controlled trial where 146 participants were randomly allocated to resistance exercise or relaxation control using block randomization stratified by baseline fatigue and age.

domain_judgments.rationale: The random allocation sequence was generated using block randomization, but there is no information provided regarding allocation concealment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Group allocation was performed using predetermined lists with block randomisation and stratification by baseline physical fatigue level and age.

domain_judgments.rationale: Blinding of participants and personnel was not possible for this behavioral exercise intervention, and the analysis was explicitly per-protocol/complete-case excluding dropouts rather than intention-to-treat.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: SAS (v9.3) was used for statistical analysis based on ANCOVA test on the per protocol. The complete-case analyses were performed.

domain_judgments.rationale: Attrition was low and balanced between groups (8/73 [11%] in resistance exercise vs 6/73 [8%] in relaxation control), making it unlikely to meaningfully bias the findings.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: 146 patients were randomised using block randomization with age and baseline fatigue-level randomisation and allocated to perform resistance exercise or relaxation control (n = 73 for each group). After the 12-week chemoradiotherapy, 65 and 67 patients in the resistance exercise and relaxation control group respectively completed the study and underwent post-intervention assessments.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes such as fatigue and quality of life are self-reported by unblinded participants who were fully aware of whether they received the active resistance exercise or relaxation intervention.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Cancer-related fatigue, which encompassed general fatigue, physical fatigue, emotional fatigue, mental fatigue and vigour, was assessed using the MFSI-SF scoring system (Pien et al., 2011). Quality of life was assessed by patients using self-reported score using the EORTC QLQ-30 form...

domain_judgments.rationale: No trial pre-registration or published statistical analysis plan is mentioned, leaving open the possibility of selective outcome reporting or analysis choices.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The aim of the randomised clinical study was to investigate the benefits of resistance exercise during chemoradiotherapy in NPC patients.

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is high, primarily driven by the lack of participant blinding on purely subjective, self-reported outcomes (fatigue and quality of life) along with a per-protocol analysis strategy.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly allocated 1:1 to the exercise group or relaxation control group using predetermined lists with random block size, stratified by age and baseline physical fatigue.

domain_judgments.rationale: Random allocation was generated by a biostatistician uninvolved in recruitment using random block sizes, stratified by age and physical fatigue, with concealment maintained.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Allocation was performed by a biostatistician uninvolved in recruitment, based on predetermined lists with random block size, stratified by age and baseline physical fatigue level. Other study personnel did not have access to the randomization lists.

domain_judgments.rationale: An active control group with identical contact time was used, adherence was balanced, deviations were minimal, and an appropriate ITT analysis was conducted.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Both interventions were performed for 60 min twice weekly over 12 weeks together with other cancer patients under the supervision and guidance of experienced therapists in specific training facilities... Median attendance was similar in both groups, with 17 out of 24 scheduled sessions attended (71%...).

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for 95 of 99 eligible participants (over 95%), missingness was minimal and balanced across arms, and sensitivity analyses via multiple imputation showed robust results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of 101 randomized breast cancer patients, 97 (96%) reached the postintervention assessment of the primary outcome (Fig. 1). Two patients had to be excluded from analysis, because they started chemotherapy after baseline. Thus, the analysis included n = 95 patients... As very few fatigue values were missing (3%), we performed complete-case analyses. Sensitivity analyses using multiple imputation algorithms (SAS PROC MI and MIANALYSE)... yielded no substantial changes in the results.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were self-reported participant-reported measures (fatigue and quality of life) in an unblinded behavioral intervention trial, meaning participants' awareness of assignment could plausibly influence their reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Fatigue was self-assessed using the validated 20- item multidimensional Fatigue Assessment Questionnaire (FAQ), which covers the dimensions physical, affective and cognitive fatigue. Scores were derived by adding the answers... and linearly rescaling to a 0– 100 scale... QoL was self-assessed using the validated 30- item EORTC QLQ-C30 (version 3.0).

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT01106820) and reported outcomes according to a pre-specified analysis plan, including the primary endpoint of total fatigue.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study was approved by the ethics committee of the University of Heidelberg and registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT01106820)... The primary endpoint was change in total fatigue from pre- to postintervention... Besides the primary endpoint total fatigue, we conducted a priori planned analyses on the three different fatigue dimensions.

overall_summary: While the trial demonstrated rigorous randomization, good adherence, minimal attrition, and adherence to a pre-specified protocol, some concerns remain due to the reliance on participant-reported subjective outcomes (fatigue and quality of life) in an unblinded behavioral intervention study.

design_rationale: The study is described as a randomized controlled trial in which participants were stratified and randomized into two parallel intervention arms (POWIR resistance training vs. FLEX stretching control).

domain_judgments.rationale: Although stratified block randomization occurred after baseline testing, specific methods of random sequence generation and allocation concealment are not reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization was stratified by length of ADT use (>1 or <1 year) and current aerobic activity (≥ vs <90 min/week) and occurred after baseline testing. Sample sizes were uneven between groups because enrollment ceased prior to completing a randomization block of 20 participants.

domain_judgments.rationale: An active stretching control was used to balance attention and expectations, and analyses were conducted using an intention-to-treat approach via linear mixed-effects models.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Tests were administered by trained technicians blinded to group assignment. ... A gentle exercise placebo group was used as a control rather than a usual care group to equalize attention, maximize retention and minimize contamination.

domain_judgments.rationale: There was differential attrition (10% vs 25%) and missingness was likely related to true health status, raising some concerns despite mixed-effects modeling.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Over the 12 months, 6 men withdrew from the study and 2 were lost to follow-up yielding retention rates of 90% in POWIR and 75% in FLEX (Fig 1). Final data were not available for 5 men due to disease recurrence (N=4) or poor health (N=1)... Missing data may not have been missing at random (MAR) because disease recurrence and poor health could be related to poorer strength and functional outcomes.

domain_judgments.rationale: Objective outcome assessors were blinded, and self-report measures used standardized validated instruments in a trial with an active attention-matched control group.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Tests were administered by trained technicians blinded to group assignment. ... Self-report physical function was measured using three separate instruments...

domain_judgments.rationale: The paper reports on multiple secondary outcomes and subscales from three different physical function instruments without a detailed prespecified analysis plan, raising some concern for selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The purpose of this paper is to report on secondary endpoints of that study, including muscle strength, physical function and disability. ... Clinical trial registration number: NCT00660686

overall_summary: The study is judged to have some concerns overall due to missing details on sequence generation and allocation concealment, differential attrition with health-related missingness, and reporting of multiple secondary functional subscales.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly allocated to either the resistance exercise intervention group or the waiting list control group using a table of random numbers stratified by center and treatment intent.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was generated using random number tables, allocation was concealed from study staff until baseline testing was complete, and baseline characteristics were well-balanced across groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization, performed using a table of random numbers, was stratified according to center (Ottawa or Edmonton) and intent of treatment (curative or palliative)... The treatment allocation was concealed from the study coordinator until completion of baseline testing and stratification.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although participants could not be blinded to the exercise intervention, the trial analyzed participants according to their assigned groups (intention-to-treat) with high adherence and no indication of substantial non-protocol interventions affecting the comparison.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: No blinding of patients was used in treatment group assignment, and they were immediately informed about their group assignment... All patients randomly assigned to receive treatment were included in the intent-to-treat analysis.

domain_judgments.rationale: Attrition was 12.9% overall (9.8% intervention vs 16.4% control) and handled via baseline observation carried forward (LOCF) for a deteriorating/changing condition, which may introduce bias into the treatment effect estimate.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: During the intervention period, eight men (9.8%) dropped out in the intervention group compared with 12 men (16.4%) in the control group (P = .79). Overall, end-oftreatment (12-week) data were available for 135 of 155 men (87.1%)... If data were missing because of loss to follow-up, information from the participant’s baseline evaluation was used in the analysis, on the basis of the last observation carried forward principle.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcomes (fatigue and quality of life) are participant-reported, and participants were unblinded to their assignment to an active exercise intervention versus a waitlist control, creating a risk that outcome reporting was influenced by awareness of assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcomes were fatigue and disease-specific quality of life as assessed by self-reported questionnaires after 12 weeks... Blinding was used for data collection. A research assistant with no knowledge of group assignment collected muscular fitness and anthropometric data and scored questionnaire responses.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary and secondary outcome measures and statistical analyses were clearly prespecified and reported as planned according to standard instruments.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: For the primary analysis, a t test was used to compare between-group changes in fatigue (fatigue scale) and disease-specific quality of life (FACT-P) between baseline and 12 weeks.

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is judged as 'some concerns' due to the unblinded participant-reported nature of the primary subjective outcomes (fatigue and quality of life) comparing an active exercise program to a waitlist control, along with reliance on last observation carried forward for missing data.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly assigned to one of three groups (aerobic exercise, resistance exercise, or usual care) using a computer-generated random allocation program stratified by center and chemotherapy protocol.
overall_summary: The study was a well-conducted randomized controlled trial with central allocation concealment, high follow-up (>92%), and intention-to-treat analyses. However, some concerns arise in domain 4 because the primary and key secondary outcomes are self-reported patient-rated measures assessed by participants who could not be blinded to exercise intervention assignment.

design_rationale: The study is explicitly described as a randomized controlled trial in which participants were randomly assigned to resistance training, aerobic training, or usual care using computer-generated numbers and central random assignment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Randomization was generated using computer-generated numbers with central random assignment and allocation concealment, and baseline characteristics were well-balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants were stratified by intended duration of ADT ( 16 weeks/ none v ADT  16 weeks) and randomly assigned to one of three groups: resistance training, aerobic training, or usual care using computer-generated numbers. Central random assignment was used, with allocation concealment before assignment. To ensure blinding of the research coordinator, an exercise specialist handled the random assignments.

domain_judgments.rationale: Due to the nature of the exercise intervention, participants could not be blinded, and some non-protocol exercise contamination (drop-ins) occurred across groups, though intention-to-treat analysis was performed.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: For all analyses, an intention-to-treat approach was followed. [...] Overall, 18 (15%) of 121 participants reported regular exercise outside treatment group assignment...

domain_judgments.rationale: Retention was high (92.6% complete follow-up), reasons and rates of loss to follow-up were balanced across groups, and mixed models were utilized.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The follow-up assessment rate for our primary end point of fatigue was 92.6%. [...] We obtained follow-up data from 112 (92.6%) of 121 participants. Loss to follow-up was similar between groups. Mixed-model repeated measures analysis was used to compare the differences between groups over time.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome (fatigue via FACT-Fatigue) and QOL are self-reported by participants who were aware of their assignment to exercise versus usual care, which could influence their subjective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patient-rated outcomes were assessed at baseline before commencement of radiotherapy, in the middle (12 weeks), and at the end of intervention (24 weeks). Fatigue, PCa-specific, and cancer-specific QOL were assessed by the Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy–Fatigue (FACT-Fatigue), Prostate (FACT-P), and General (FACT-G) scales, respectively.

domain_judgments.rationale: Analyses followed an a priori analysis plan with pre-specified primary and secondary endpoints and contrast testing without signs of selective outcome reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: For the patient-rated outcomes assessed at baseline, midpoint, and postintervention, we used contrasts defined a priori to examine changes between baseline and midpoint (12 weeks) and baseline and post-test (24 weeks) for each outcome and to compare group differences in mean change (resistance v usual care and aerobic v usual care).

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns, driven primarily by the lack of participant blinding inherent to an exercise intervention evaluating self-reported patient outcomes such as fatigue and quality of life.

design_rationale: The study is described as a randomized controlled trial in which participants were allocated to conditions using a 2:1 block randomization scheme with a computerized random-number generator.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants were allocated using computerized random-number generation with block randomization stratified by age and sex managed by an independent statistician, ensuring adequate sequence generation and concealment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Allocation to one of the RT groups depended on the living distance from the study center. Patients living close to the study center (about <20 km) who were able to regularly visit our training facility were randomized to the supervised progressive RT group (RT1) or the control group (CON), whereas patients living farther away were assigned to the home-based progressive RT group (RT2) or CON. A 2:1 block randomization with a computerized random-number generator was used to allocate patients to the corresponding groups. Thus, CON included patients from all living distances in proportion to the exercising patients. Randomization was stratified by sex and age and was done by an independent statistician.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although blinding of participants to exercise interventions is not possible, the intervention was administered according to protocol without evidence of non-protocol deviations affecting trial outcomes, and analyses adhered to an intention-to-treat principle.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Differences among the groups with changes in physical fitness from preintervention to postintervention on an intent-to-treat basis were conducted with analyses of covariance. We used changes in parameters of muscle strength and cardiorespiratory fitness from preintervention to postintervention as dependent variables and intervention group as independent variable.

domain_judgments.rationale: Substantial outcome data were missing (over 33% of randomized patients were excluded from the primary fitness and strength analyses), and no imputation methods or sensitivity analyses addressing potential bias from missingness were performed.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In total, 65 (21.4%) of 304 eligible PC patients gave written informed consent and were randomized after baseline assessment, 12 patients to RT1, 31 to RT2, and 22 patients to CON (Fig. 1). All 65 patients completed baseline assessments, and 48 patients (73.8%) completed the 6-month intervention phase. Reasons for premature dropout were withdrawal (n = 11), disease progression (n = 3), and death (n = 3). Group specific dropout rates were 25% in RT1, 29% in RT2, and 23% in CON. Preintervention and postintervention assessments of muscle strength and cardiorespiratory fitness were available in a total of 43 patients (66.2%).

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were assessed using objective, standardized physiological devices and protocols that are unlikely to be biased by knowledge of group assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Muscle strength was assessed with an isokinetic dynamometer (IsoMed2000; D&R Ferstl GmbH, Hemau, Germany)... Additionally, we measured the MVIC with handheld dynamometry (HHD) (Citec, Haren, Groningen, the Netherlands) using a standardized test protocol... Cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) was used for assessing cardiorespiratory fitness.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered (NCT01977066), and outcomes and prespecified analytical strategies were reported consistently according to plan.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: As the presented analyses on muscle strength and cardiorespiratory fitness were exploratory, no adjustment for multiple testing was performed... The study was approved by the ethics committee of the Medical Faculty of Heidelberg University (S-409/2013) and has been registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT01977066).

overall_summary: The study is judged at high overall risk of bias due to significant missing outcome data, with only 43 of 65 randomized patients (66.2%) providing postintervention physical fitness and strength outcome data without appropriate handling of missingness in the analyses.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly allocated 1:1 to an intervention or control group using a computer-assisted pseudo-random number generator and sealed opaque envelopes.
overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is judged as high due to substantial missing outcome data (38% dropout rate leading to complete exclusion of over a third of randomized participants from the primary analysis) and the use of a per-protocol analysis in an unblinded exercise trial.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly allocated in a 1:1:1 ratio using computer-generated random numbers.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was computer-generated, but there is no description of allocation concealment and the principal investigator directly allocated the subjects.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Included subjects were randomly assigned in a 1:1:1 manner, using computer-generated numbers (JMP Pro 12 software), to either HIIT, RES or UC groups... The principal investigator (PI) allocated the subjects.

domain_judgments.rationale: Blinding of participants and personnel was not possible due to the nature of the exercise interventions, and although an intention-to-treat analysis was stated, six randomized patients who dropped out before baseline testing/intervention were excluded from the analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Six of them who never showed up for the baseline testing and intervention were considered as “early dropouts” and were not included in the analyses. Seventy-two PCa patients completed the study.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for all 72 participants who commenced the trial (100% completion rate among those starting), and the early dropouts occurred equally across groups prior to receiving any intervention.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Among the 84 potentially eligible patients, 78 subjects were randomized (Fig. 2). Six of them who never showed up for the baseline testing and intervention were considered as “early dropouts” and were not included in the analyses. Seventy-two PCa patients completed the study.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome (cancer-treatment-related fatigue) is a participant-reported subjective outcome, participants were fully aware of their assigned intervention group, and outcome assessors were unblinded, introducing high risk of detection bias for self-reported measures.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome was CTRF evaluated with the Functional Assessment of Chronic Illness Therapy–Fatigue (FACIT-F)... All questionnaires were self-reported and objectively measured variables were collected by the PI... Firstly, there was no blind assessor to evaluate outcomes.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered at clinicaltrials.gov (NCT03252821) and all pre-specified outcomes and analyses are reported consistent with the protocol.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This study was registered at clinicaltrials.gov (NCT03252821) and follow the CONSORT guidelines

overall_summary: The study is at overall high risk of bias driven primarily by Domain 4, as the primary outcome (cancer-treatment-related fatigue) was subjective and self-reported by unblinded participants aware of their active exercise or usual care control assignment, alongside lack of allocation concealment reporting in Domain 1.
